To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we design and analyze centralized and distributed algorithms that reduce the communication cost for executing spatial queries in a sensor network by constructing a connected sensor cover.

we develop a centralized approximation algorithm for constructing a topology involving a connected sensor cover, and we develop two distributed self-organization algorithms, one with a guarantee on the size, and the other without any guarantee.

we have designed algorithms for self-organization of a wireless sensor network into a connected topology that involves a small subset of sensors, and that our approaches can result in significant reduction in the communication cost incurred for execution of queries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing efficient algorithms that exploit the spatial redundancy within a sensor network to construct a connected sensor cover, which can be used for efficient spatial query processing.
the problem of efficient query processing using self-organization of a large-scale sensor network.
reducing communication cost in spatial query execution by self-organizing the network into a connected sensor cover.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we develop algorithms for efficient self-organization of the sensor network in response to a spatial query to reduce communication cost and hence energy consumption.
we design algorithms for self-organization of a wireless sensor network to reduce the communication costs incurred in query processing.
we develop a new approach to self-organization of a wireless sensor network for efficient query execution, and design and evaluate several algorithms for such self-organization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we develop the notion and algorithms for self-organization of a wireless sensor network to reduce the communication energy consumption.
we design and analyze approximation algorithms for self-organization of a large sensor network into a small topology that involves only the sensors necessary to execute a spatial query.
we have developed the notion of connected sensor cover for efficient spatial query execution in sensor networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a sensor network can self-organize itself to construct a connected sensor cover, and use the cover for efficient spatial query execution.
the self-organization of the sensor network can be a very effective approach to reduce energy consumption, especially for long-running queries.
the self-organization of a network into a topology involving a connected sensor cover can significantly improve energy efficiency in sensor network queries.
